raw_response:
Aiyo, you want me to tell you what I'll do this year? Alright, let me think…

I've been on this land since I was a little girl — my mother taught me, and her mother taught her. Four mu and a bit, that's what we've got. Just me and one other at home, and sometimes he's off working in town, so I can't be running around doing fancy things. Whatever I do, I need to be able to do it myself or with a little help from my neighbor's boy when I pay him some.

**Wheat first, because that's what goes in now… well, went in last October.**

I planted around National Day time, maybe a few days after, like always. Used seed I bought at the shop — the same kind everyone around here plants, I don't remember the name, the shopkeeper knows. Before planting I spread one bag of the compound fertilizer (the one with three numbers on it, 50 jin bag… no wait, 100 jin, one bag) across the whole field. That's about half a bag per two mu, you know. Then after the New Year when the wheat starts standing up again and turning green, if it looks a little yellow I'll scatter some urea — maybe half a bag across all of it. My neighbor auntie does the same.

For water — I'll turn on the well pump maybe three times. Once after winter when it warms up (the返青水, the "green-up water"), once when it's heading out, and once when the grain is filling if the sky doesn't give us rain. The pump costs money, so I don't water more than I need. If it rains good, I skip one.

Pests — usually I spray once for the aphids when they show up on the heads, and sometimes a weed spray in spring if the field looks bad. Harvest in June, I hire the combine machine that goes village to village — costs maybe 50 yuan per mu but what can you do, I can't cut four mu by hand anymore, my back.

**Then maize, right after.**

The minute wheat comes off, maize has to go in. No time to waste — a week at most or it's too late. I don't plow, just have someone come rotary-till quick, or sometimes the no-till planter goes straight in with the seed and a little fertilizer together. One bag of compound at planting, same as wheat. Then when it's about waist-high, before it tassels, I scatter urea again — maize is hungry, eats more than wheat. Maybe a full bag across the field.

Irrigate once or twice if July-August is dry, but usually the rains come and I don't need to water much. Spray once for the borer worm if I see the leaves getting chewed. Harvest late September, by hand mostly because the plot is small — my cousin helps, I give him some grain.

Yield? Last year wheat gave me around 400 jin per mu I think, maize a bit more, maybe 450. This year, who knows — depends on the weather. I don't count chickens.

Cash is tight, always. I buy fertilizer when I have money from selling last harvest. If prices go up at the shop I might buy one less bag and hope the wheat still does okay. Better safe than sorry though — skimping on fertilizer is how you get a bad year.
